ACADEMIC REGULATIONS: ATTENDANCE NORMS & ELIGIBILITY
1. Minimum Attendance Requirement for Appearing in Examinations
As laid down under University of Mumbai Ordinance 6086 and NEP 2020 guidelines, regular attendance across all
scheduled academic components is strictly compulsory.
What is the minimum attendance required to appear for exams? Every student registered in an undergraduate
engineering program is required to maintain a minimum attendance of 75% in each individual theory subject, tutorial,
and laboratory practical session throughout the semester.
- Attendance Calculation: Attendance percentage is calculated from the

ry subject, tutorial,
and laboratory practical session throughout the semester.
- Attendance Calculation: Attendance percentage is calculated from the date of commencement of term until the last
official instructional day.
- Monthly Defaulter Tracking: Defaulter lists are compiled and displayed on departmental notice boards on the 5th day
of every calendar month.
- Parental Intimation: Automated SMS alerts and formal letters are dispatched to parents/guardians when cumulative
attendance drops below 75%.
2. Defaulter Categories and Warning Tiers
- Category A (75% and Above): Satisfactory attendance status. The candidate is unconditionally eligible for term grant
and all internal/external semester end examinations.
- Category B (60% to 74%): Caution status / First warning. Student along with

ible for term grant
and all internal/external semester end examinations.
- Category B (60% to 74%): Caution status / First warning. Student along with parents must attend an academic
counseling session with the class advisor and HOD.
- Category C (Below 60%): Critical defaulter. The candidate is in violation of Mumbai University rules and is liable to be
debarred from writing exams.

3. Condonation of Attendance on Medical and Special Grounds
Under exceptional situations where a student's attendance falls between 60% and 74%, condonation of attendance
shortage up to a maximum of 15% may be granted by the College Academic Committee subject to:
- Medical Illness Condonation: Genuine hospitalization or severe illness verified by an authentic medical certificate
signed by a registered medical practitioner (MBBS minimum) submitted within 7 working days of recovery.
- Institutional Representation: Prior written sanction from the Principal for representing Atharva College of Engineering
or the University of Mum

ry.
- Institutional Representation: Prior written sanction from the Principal for representing Atharva College of Engineering
or the University of Mumbai in recognized sports tournaments, technical hackathons, or youth festivals.
4. Debarment and Academic Consequences
Students whose final attendance remains strictly below 75% without authorized condonation will be officially debarred
from taking the semester end theory and practical examinations.
A debarred student will not receive term grant for the respective semester and will be required to re-register as a
repeater student during the following academic year, fulfilling all laboratory and lecture obligations anew.

SCHOLARSHIP & FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE NOTIFICATION
1. Available Scholarship Schemes (AY 2025-2026)
Atharva College of Engineering assists students in securing various State Government, Central Government, and
Institutional financial assistance schemes:
- Rajarshi Shahu Maharaj Scheme (EBC): 50% tuition and exam fee concession for eligible students admitted via CAP
with annual family income up to Rs. 8 Lakhs.
- Social Justice Welfare Scholarships: 100% tuition and development fee reimbursement for SC/ST students, and 50%
for OBC/VJNT/SBC category candidates.
- Minority Scholarship Schemes: Direct government financial allowanc

e reimbursement for SC/ST students, and 50%
for OBC/VJNT/SBC category candidates.
- Minority Scholarship Schemes: Direct government financial allowance for Muslim, Christian, Buddhist, Sikh, Parsi,
and Jain students.
2. How Can I Apply for a Scholarship? (Procedure)
Students must strictly follow these five steps to apply for scholarship benefits:
- Step 1: MahaDBT Registration: Open an account on the Government of Maharashtra scholarship portal at
mahadbt.maharashtra.gov.in using your Aadhaar number and OTP verification.
- Step 2: Profile Completion: Fill personal details, permanent address, caste particulars, and upload photograph and
signature.
- Step 3: College & Course Selection: Select Atharva College of Engineering (Institute Code: 3203), choose Electronics
& Computer Science, and in

2. Detailed Module Outline for Core Subjects
- Microcontroller Applications: Instruction sets and architecture of ARM Cortex-M and 8051 controllers, timer and
interrupt handling, GPIO interfacing, serial protocols (UART, SPI, I2C), PWM generation, and embedded C firmware design.
- Database Management Systems (DBMS): Relational database concepts, ER diagrams, SQL DDL/DML, functional
dependencies, normalization (1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF), indexing (B-trees, hashing), transaction processing, ACID properties,
concurrency control, and introductory NoSQL databases.
- Signals and Systems: Continuous and discrete-time signals, Linear T

cessing, ACID properties,
concurrency control, and introductory NoSQL databases.
- Signals and Systems: Continuous and discrete-time signals, Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) systems, Fourier transform,
Laplace transform, Z-transform, frequency response, and digital filter fundamentals.
3. Examination Evaluation and Credit Award Pattern
- Internal Assessment (IA): Two internal unit tests of 20 marks each; the average score of both tests is incorporated into
final grade calculation.
- End Semester Examination (ESE): University theory paper of 80 marks with a duration of 3 hours covering all six
syllabus modules.
- Term Work (TW) & Oral Exam: 25 marks term work based on journal submission and mini project defense evaluated
jointly by external and internal examiners.
